objective: AGENTS.md carried two false statements about itself. Section 3 step 7 (#348) instructed a bare `python3` command; on Windows that resolves to a non-functional Microsoft Store alias, so an agent executing the mandatory resume protocol literally there must silently substitute a command the record never names. Section 10.3 (#361) asserted 'Twenty-seven of the twenty-eight tracked pages' under four named directories; `control/index.html` landed under `control/` in WP-113 and the true count is 29, so both halves were wrong. Step 7 now names the requirement - a Python 3 interpreter - and shows both invocations, `python3` on POSIX and `python` on Windows, with one sentence recording that `.github/workflows/pages.yml`'s own `python3` is correct on `ubuntu-latest` and is not to be 'fixed' to match. Section 10.3's count is deleted rather than corrected to 29, naming the command and the validator's existing live output instead.
completed: DEFECT 1 (#348) REPAIRED. AGENTS.md section 3 step 7 no longer instructs a bare `python3` command. It now reads: 'Run the validator's own self-tests, then `scripts/validate_continuity.py`, with a Python 3 interpreter: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` then `python3 scripts/validate_continuity.py` on POSIX; `python -m unittest discover -s tests` then `python scripts/validate_continuity.py` on Windows, where `python3` resolves to a non-functional Microsoft Store alias.' - naming the requirement and showing both invocations, per #348's first option, with no runner script added and no path hardcoded to one machine.

STEP 7 WAS EXECUTED AS NEWLY WRITTEN, ON THIS MACHINE, BOTH COMMANDS. `python -m unittest discover -s tests` ran 396 tests OK (skipped=1); `python scripts/validate_continuity.py` printed CONTINUITY_VALIDATION=PASS. Both use the interpreter this machine actually has; neither prints the Store-alias sentence #348 measured.

.github/workflows/pages.yml WAS READ, NOT EDITED, AND VERIFIED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST. Its `python3` invocations sit at lines 46 ('Prove the validator fails closed'), 49 ('Validate continuity contracts') and 91 ('Project the records into the staged control page'), all on `run: ubuntu-latest`, where `python3` is the real interpreter and the build is green. AGENTS.md step 7 now says so in one sentence, so the next reader does not 'fix' CI to match the old wording.

DEFECT 2 (#361) REPAIRED BY DELETION, NOT CORRECTION. AGENTS.md section 10.3 no longer states a page count. `git ls-files '*.html' | wc -l` on this branch is 29 (measured after every edit in this package, since none add or remove a tracked *.html file); section 10.3 now names that command and notes that `scripts/validate_continuity.py` already prints the same figure as `PASS: html-pages:<n>` on every run - verified: this run printed `PASS: html-pages:29`. Correcting the sentence to 'twenty-nine' would have been true today and stale at the next page, exactly as #361 itself went stale once already; deleting the hand-maintained number is the ruling the brief already made.

THE GUARD, tests/test_resume_protocol_command.py, covers defect 1 only, scoped to the command string rather than the sentence: a line in section 3 naming `python3` without also naming the bare `python` form and the word `Windows` on that same line fails. test_anchors_exist asserts the section-3 heading is present and that the section still mentions python3 or python at all, so the guard cannot pass by finding nothing. Defect 2 gets no guard, by design: its repair deletes the hand-maintained number, and a deleted claim cannot drift - there is nothing left to ratchet.

THREE CONTROLS in scripts/wp116_controls.py, on fresh copies, unmutated copy first and green: (1) step 7 reverted to the pre-fix bare `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` text turns test_no_bare_python3_command red, isolated - the exact control #348's own brief names by name; (2) a second, correctly-paired POSIX/Windows sentence added elsewhere in section 3 leaves the suite GREEN, proving the guard checks the pairing rather than rationing every mention of the word python3; (3) renaming the section-3 heading turns test_anchors_exist red, isolated, proving the anchor is asserted rather than assumed. None of the three trips more than the test named for it.

THE OTHER 18 OCCURRENCES SURVEYED, CLASSIFIED, NOT LEFT UNEXAMINED. `git grep -o "python3 " -- '*.md' '*.html' | wc -l` is 19, measured before AND after this package's edits (19 both times, since no edit removes or duplicates the substring `python3 ` - wording was added around existing occurrences, not multiplied). Per file: README.md 5, docs/LIVE_PREVIEW.md 6, index.html 2, docs/experiments/fixtures/README.md 2, docs/NEXT_STEPS.md 1, .github/pull_request_template.md 1, AGENTS.md 2. The two on AGENTS.md's own line 30 are defect 1, fixed above. Of the other 17: FIVE CHANGED to match section 3's resolution, each a bare, platform-unqualified instruction with no Windows sibling anywhere nearby, mirroring the exact defect shape - README.md's 'Agent continuity' step 6 (2 occurrences), README.md's 'Validate before every handoff' fenced block (2 occurrences, now split into a POSIX block and a Windows block), and .github/pull_request_template.md's Continuity row (1 occurrence, now naming both forms in one cell). TWELVE LEFT, explicitly, each for its own reason: README.md line 24 and five of docs/LIVE_PREVIEW.md's six (lines 105, 120, 144, 181, 202) are already OS-branched, each paired with a working `py`/`python` Windows alternative shown in the same section, OR (lines 181 and 202 specifically) already resolved by that same document's own Troubleshooting entry '### `python3: command not found`' two subsections above, which already tells a Windows reader to use `py` or `python`; docs/LIVE_PREVIEW.md line 241 and docs/NEXT_STEPS.md line 38 are evidence-record fields (one a forward template, one a specific dated past verification already executed) rather than instructions to execute now; docs/experiments/fixtures/README.md's two occurrences invoke a different tool entirely (the WP-024 fixtures' `build.py`, unrelated to the resume protocol); index.html's two occurrences (the local-preview demo and the 'First safe command for every new session' display) are left as a published-artifact scope boundary - the brief's own caution against a blanket rewrite touching a published HTML page, weighed against the fact that index.html carries no Windows alternative anywhere on the page for either command, which is recorded here as an open tension rather than resolved silently. Full per-line reasoning is in the session report.

NO RULE CHANGED. Both defects were statements of fact that were false; making a false statement true is not a policy change. No obligation in AGENTS.md sections 1-12 was added, removed or reworded in substance - section 3's nine steps are still the same nine steps, and section 10's seven steps are still the same seven steps, one of them now naming a command instead of a number.

assumptions: That 'an instruction a reader is told to execute' is the right line between the five python3 occurrences changed and the twelve left. The ruling was made in the brief that opened this package; this package applied it to each of the 19 occurrences individually rather than re-deriving the rule, and recorded its reasoning per occurrence so a reviewer can disagree with a specific classification rather than the rule itself.

That leaving index.html's two occurrences unrepaired is the right side of that same line, given the brief's caution against a blanket rewrite touching a published HTML page. This is recorded as an open tension in 'remaining' rather than resolved by assumption, because the occurrences are, on their own wording, the same unqualified-instruction shape as the five that were changed.

That AGENTS.md sections 1-12 were not altered in substance by either repair. Both changes replace a false factual claim with a true one inside an existing numbered step; no step was added, removed, renumbered or reworded as an obligation. If a reviewer reads either change as narrowing or widening what an agent MUST do, that reading should stop this package rather than be argued past, per the brief's own instruction.
